alalal-e82902-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 16: how the kinds of vision relate to the heaven into which Paul was caught up.

alalal-e82902-d1e115.summary: Introduces the question on Augustine's words in Lombard's text: not bodily, not imaginatively, but intellectually.

alalal-e82902-d1e127.summary: First question: all the kinds of vision listed earlier seem to reduce to the three named here.

alalal-e82902-d1e139.summary: Second question: Augustine in De Genesi ad litteram XII, cited in the Gloss on 2 Corinthians 12, calls these three kinds of vision the three heavens into which Paul was caught up; what conformity do they have to heaven?

alalal-e82902-d1e163.summary: Reply to the first: divided by the modes of visible things there are the six general modes; divided by the parts of the seeing soul there are only three: external, bodily vision through the senses; or internal, either bodily, imaginative vision, or intelligible, intellectual vision.
claims: By the powers of the soul, vision is corporeal, imaginative or intellectual.

alalal-e82902-d1e189.summary: Reply to the second: these visions are called heaven not in every way but when heaven is opened in them, i.e. heavenly secrets are revealed: to sense, as angels revealed to Abraham the promised seed; to imagination, as to Ezekiel in the living creatures; and to intellect, as to Daniel and Joseph, who received understanding of visions. Only the last opens heaven simply, the others only in a qualified way, as only intellectual vision is prophecy simply, the others only insofar as understanding is needed in the vision (Damascene).
claims: The three visions are 'heavens' when heavenly secrets are revealed through them, and only intellectual vision opens heaven simply.

alalal-e82902.summary: Article 16 relates Augustine's three kinds of vision (corporeal, imaginative and intellectual) to the six modes of seeing discussed before and to the three heavens of Paul's rapture. Albert explains that the six modes divide visible objects, while the three kinds divide the powers of the seeing soul: external sense, internal imagination, and intellect. These visions are called heavens when heavenly secrets are revealed in them, as to Abraham through sense, to Ezekiel through imagination, and to Daniel and Joseph through intellect. Only intellectual vision opens heaven simply, as only it is prophecy in the full sense.
claims: Vision is corporeal, imaginative or intellectual according to the powers of the soul.
Each kind of vision is a 'heaven' when it reveals heavenly secrets, but only intellectual vision does so simply.
